In article <3lp6e0$d...@sif.cs.cornell.edu>, kw...@cs.cornell.edu (Alan Kwan)
wrote:

> I doubt the reasonable-ness of this ruling. Why can't I play
> a Majesty to untap just because my opponent played a Strike:
> Combat Ends? The original rules didn't say that Strike: Combat
> Ends should be resolved before strikes are /played/.

The rules state that a cobat ends happens "immediately", therefore if the
acting minion plays a combat ends type card, the combat ends before the
blocking minion can play a strike.

I would tend to agree with the desire to play another strike to cycle a
card, or for some other benifit (like playing a Majesty to untap the
blocking vampire), but the rule is pretty clear that it happens before the
blocking minion can do anything.

stephen

>The rules state that a cobat ends happens "immediately", therefore if the

>acting minion plays a combat ends type card, the combat ends before the
>blocking minion can play a strike.

The rules also state that the normal hand strike does one damage. That
damage doesn't occur until the strike resolves, however.
The rules also state that a strike to Destroy Equipment will force a piece
of equipment to be put in the owner's ash heap. That doesn't happen until
the strike resolves, however.
Dodge doesn't even prevent a First Strike from occuring - it simply
(retro-actively) cancels the effect (when the Dodge resolves, of course),
just like a Strike: Combat Ends would.

In fact, no strike has any effect until it resolves, per the rulebook.

Enter: Design Team [Groan from the audience :-]

DT: Well, looking at the text under Strike: Combat Ends (taken out of context),
The combat ends immediately upon the play of the card.
[Aside]
We'll just ignore that it says it cancels a strike with First Strike,
since now there is no strike to cancel. And we'll ignore the the fact
that the bloody entry we're taking out of context even starts with
"This is considered a strike" and "The *strike* ends combat" (Instead
of "the *declaration* of the strike ends combat", as we have
Because-We-Say-So'ed).
[Again to Captive Audience]
Hope you enjoy what used to be a logical, somewhat consistent game...

[Exeunt DT, never to be heard from again.]

>I would tend to agree with the desire to play another strike to cycle a
>card, or for some other benifit (like playing a Majesty to untap the
>blocking vampire), but the rule is pretty clear that it happens before the

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
In article <hippo-03049...@gill.hrc.utexas.edu> hi...@mail.utexas.edu (Stephen Beaulieu) writes:

>The rules state that a cobat ends happens "immediately", therefore if the
>acting minion plays a combat ends type card, the combat ends before the
>blocking minion can play a strike.

There is still the question of whether the wording is /intended/
to mean such. It can be argued that strikes (even "Combat
Ends") are not resolved until the Strike Resolution phase,
when, at that time, Combat Ends "immediately". The careless
WotC people would have written the rules that way, regardless
of which one is the /intended/ interpretation.

The rules also state, in parenthesis, "(before any damage is dealt
or any strike's effects take place)". This may even imply
that the Strike: Combat Ends is not actually resolved until the
Strike Resolution Phase, at which time it is resolved before any
other strikes or damage effects.

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <3lpgbl$e...@redwood.cs.scarolina.edu>,

sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) wrote:
> Eh? "Rules" and "Clear" in the same sentence? You shall be hanged for the
> offense, sir :-)

I guess it would be too much to hope that the DT would help to clarify
rules, rather than tending to muddy the waters considerably more. I
attempt to follow the rules to the letter, and (when possible) to the
spirit as well. But, just like in every other game, and especially in a
CCG with too many variables to completely playtest, there will be parts of
the rules where strictly following them will result in at least a modicum
of unreasonableness. Perhaps the best way to solve these problems is to
come to some sort of agreement (I know, here I go asking for miracles
again) and present them to WoTC. I am sure that among the elders of this
group, many more hours of the game have been played than the DT, (if only
because there are many more of us), and that experience would be helpful
to them. This, of course, assumes that they really care about our
opinions.

Perhaps we should look into forming an 'official' group for ruling on
complicated rules issues. At least we could be sure to have an answer
available to everybody. The DT seems to be absent or unavailable far too
often.
It's just an idea, but why not?
stephen

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <3lpkat$v...@sif.cs.cornell.edu>, kw...@cs.cornell.edu (Alan Kwan)
wrote:

> The rules also state, in parenthesis, "(before any damage is dealt
> or any strike's effects take place)". This may even imply
> that the Strike: Combat Ends is not actually resolved until the
> Strike Resolution Phase, at which time it is resolved before any
> other strikes or damage effects.

Or that wording could have been placed there to clarify that if the
blocking minion played a Strike:Combat ends, that it would not take the
effect of whatever strike was levelled against it.

I don't think we disagree on our preferred reading of the rule. I would
like a blocking minion to have a chance to play a strike card if it so
desires. I just think that going by a strict reading of the rules, and
the DTR, that it's not allowed.

As you said, this is another example of a need to clarify the wording of
the rules to make it explicit as to the method for dealing with these
cards. Unfortunately, I believe that any set of rules will have it's
ambiguities and it's unreasonable (but strictly legal) interpretations.
It's up to the players to decide to play within the spirit of the rules,
or at least to decide upon an interpretation to play with.
stephen

Immediate thoughts off the top of my head:

The way someone would 'become' one of the 'core group' would be to do what
every other one of the people mentioned above did - read the newsgroup,
answer questions, contribute reasonably to discussions and show that you
are knowledgable about the game, and stick around long enough for people
to recognize these contributions. The 'netgroup' would start with the
people mentioned above by James (plus maybe one or two others, and James
himself) and other people would be added (or could petition to be added)
based on their postings in this group.

Ideas for discussion formats:

1) Discussions between 'netgroup' on rulings gets taken to e-mail and
mailing lists. PRO - fast, needn't worry about 'cluttering up' newsgroup.
CON - too private, too inbred. Would others follow the decisions, or even
the logic of the decisions if they couldn't see the process taking place?

2) People post questions for discussion/answers (as they do now), possibly
prefacing them with a NETGROUP: header or some such. Anyone can come on
and discuss it, as it is done now, but the 'final answer' would have to be
hammered out by the netgroup members. Answer drafts could be written up
and voted on(maybe this part could be done through e-mail) and posted
after either consensus was reached (not always going to be possible) or
some majority agreed (2/3 is usually good). Those voting for and against
the final ruling could even be recorded so people could go 'on record' if
they so desired.

: How do we provide these conclusions for newbies? Can somebody keep a FAQ?

I think there would have to be one. The 'official' answers should also
be included in any such document so that people can see exactly where the
netgroup has deviated from official WotC DTRs.

I suggested something like this to Scott when I first saw his Card
Rulings file - that he add to it/keep a separate listing of 'common
sense' ways to play the cards. He begged off due to lack of time, and
suggested I do it. I started it, but it didn't get very far. I would be
willing to keep such a document should no one else volunteer for the job.

So? How does that sound?
